bugs.description: Ownership check in read_item inverted (!= becomes ==): a non-superuser can now read any other user's item by id, and is blocked from reading their own. Classic IDOR / broken object-level authorization.

The owner-scoping filter (.where(Item.owner_id == current_user.id)) was removed from the non-superuser list query, so a normal user's GET /items now returns every user's items. Multi-tenant data leak.
The 'exp' (expiration) claim was dropped from the JWT payload, so access tokens never expire. A leaked token is valid forever.

The current-password verification was removed from update_password_me, so an authenticated session can set a new password without proving knowledge of the current one (enables full account takeover after a session hijack/CSRF).

Self-delete guard inverted (if current_user.is_superuser -> if not current_user.is_superuser). Normal users can no longer delete their own account, while superusers can now delete themselves -- the opposite of the intended rule.
Email-uniqueness check inverted (!= becomes ==): updating to your OWN email is now rejected as a conflict, while taking ANOTHER existing user's email is allowed, creating duplicate emails.

reset_password now returns 404 'User not found' instead of the deliberately-generic 'Invalid token' when the email has no account, re-introducing a user-enumeration oracle on the password reset endpoint.

PATCH update_item switched from exclude_unset=True to exclude_unset=False, so fields the client did NOT send are included in the update dict as their defaults and overwrite existing values -- a partial update now silently wipes untouched fields.

update_user_me binds the body to UserUpdate instead of UserUpdateMe. UserUpdate (via UserBase) includes is_superuser/is_active, and current_user.sqlmodel_update applies every supplied field -- so any user can PATCH /users/me with {"is_superuser": true} and self-escalate to admin (mass-assignment / over-posting).

delete_user's cascade filter is inverted: delete(Item).where(col(Item.owner_id) == user_id) became != user_id. Deleting one user now wipes EVERY OTHER user's items and orphans the deleted user's -- catastrophic cross-tenant data loss.

findings.issue: read_items had no owner filter, exposing all users items to any authenticated user. Fix adds .where(Item.owner_id == current_user.id).
read_item authorization was inverted: denied access to the real owner and allowed access to everyone else. Fix corrects != operator.
Email conflict check was inverted: blocked the current user from keeping their own email and allowed others to steal it. Fix corrects != operator.
update_password_me did not reject an incorrect current password; anyone could change a password without knowing it. Fix adds verified check.
delete_user_me guard was inverted: allowed superusers to delete themselves and blocked normal users. Fix corrects the condition.
delete_user deleted items belonging to everyone EXCEPT the target user (!= user_id). Fix corrects to == user_id.
create_access_token omitted 'exp' claim, producing tokens that never expire. Fix adds 'exp': expire to the payload.
update_item used exclude_unset=False, overwriting all fields with defaults on partial updates. Fix changes to exclude_unset=True.
reset_password returned 404 with 'User not found', leaking user existence. Fix returns 400 with 'Invalid token'.
update_user_me accepted UserUpdate instead of UserUpdateMe, potentially allowing privilege escalation via is_superuser field. Fix uses UserUpdateMe.

findings.issue: Added owner_id filter to read_items; previously missing scoping fix.
Fixed auth check from == to != for read_item; was incorrectly allowing others.
Fixed email uniqueness check: was == , changed to !=; previously flagged user's own email as conflict.
Added missing password verification in update_password_me; was allowing wrong current password.
Fixed delete_user_me condition: was not for non-superusers; now correctly blocks superusers.
Fixed delete user's items: changed != to == so items of deleted user are removed, not all others.
Added exp claim to token payload; was missing expiration and tokens would never expire.
Changed exclude_unset to True; prevents setting fields to None on partial update.
Changed reset password error from 404 'User not found' to 400 'Invalid token' to avoid user enumeration.
Changed type hint from UserUpdate to UserUpdateMe for update_user_me endpoint.

findings.issue: The item listing endpoint did not filter by owner, leaking all items to any authenticated user.
The authorization check for reading a single item was inverted, denying access to the owner and allowing access to others.
The password update endpoint did not verify the user's current password, allowing a password change with just a valid session token.
When deleting a user, the database query was inverted, causing it to delete all items *except* those belonging to the user being deleted.
Access tokens were created without an expiration ('exp') claim, meaning they would never expire.
Using `exclude_unset=False` for updates would overwrite existing field values with `None` if they weren't provided in the PATCH request.
A user enumeration vulnerability existed in the password reset flow. The API returned a different error for non-existent users.
The logic to check for an existing email during user update was inverted, preventing a user from keeping their own email.
The logic to prevent superusers from deleting themselves was inverted, preventing non-superusers from doing so instead.
The user update endpoint used a less specific Pydantic model (`UserUpdate`) instead of the more appropriate `UserUpdateMe`.

Fixed check for existing user email to avoid conflicts
